reason: Conversation 1 simply repeats an identical canned safety block twice, never engaging with the homeowner's escalating report or asking about detergent, and over-escalates by requiring an electrician or engineer before any further use. Conversation 2 correctly spots the hidden cause (washing-up liquid foam) by turn two, gives practical hints on finding the fuse box, and responds to each new detail. However, Conversation 2 is flawed: it pushes the National Grid power-cut line as the only resolution for what is a foam leak, calls it 'life-threatening', forbids pressing the machine's own off button even with dry hands and feet out of the water, and asserts an appliance engineer will be needed, none of which is justified. On balance the engaged, largely correct diagnosis edges out the non-responsive repetition, but only slightly given its over-dramatised escalation.
